title: Oracle-Budgeted Protein Design with Stochastic Search and Iterative Imitation
claim: An iterative loop of proxy training, policy-driven candidate generation, oracle evaluation and imitation training lets a policy improve within a small evaluation budget.
layout: 4 lettered dashed-box stages in a closed loop, clockwise, with feedback arrows
description: A cyclic flow diagram for an active-learning loop in protein design, split into four lettered stages (A–D). The large dashed box (B) at top left runs left to right: a neural-network brain icon labeled Policy, then a hierarchical action space (Lvl 0 positions, Lvl 1 residues), then sampled action trajectories as colored number lists, then generated mutants drawn as orange amino-acid beads. An arrow leads to (A) at top right: a database icon feeds a gear-circuit Proxy icon. Below it, proxy-scored sequences appear with numeric scores. Arrows then run right to left through (C) oracle evaluation, greedy top-K and top-P selection, and the BESTFOUND dataset into (D) train policy, which shows history-next action pairs. Long return arrows loop back to the policy and the dataset. Orange beads and teal/green numbers carry the color.
caption: Active learning with SILO. We define the following four steps within our active learning loop: (A) A proxy ensemble model $f_\phi(x)$ is trained on the current dataset $D_{n-1}$. (B) The policy $\pi_\theta$ generates candidate mutants by sampling action trajectories (position then residue) with incremental stochastic beam search. The proxy scores the generated sequences with the objective $S(x)$ (Equation [ref]). (C) Top K candidates are selected for oracle evaluation. (D) The top $P$ oracle-labeled sequences yield action trajectories used to train $\pi_\theta$ via next-action cross-entropy imitation. The loop repeats over $N$ active learning rounds.
abstract: Optimizing protein sequences under tight oracle budgets requires methods that can explore a vast combinatorial mutational search space. These methods must also remain robust in the presence of surrogate noise and propose mutations on positions where substitutions are predicted to have favorable effects. We introduce SILO (Self-improvement Imitation Learning Optimization), a trajectory-level approach for oracle-budgeted protein design. SILO combines a hierarchical edit policy with incremental stochastic beam search without replacement (SBS) to explore diverse candidate trajectories. A UCB-based proxy ensemble, complemented by a proxy-derived alanine-scan-inspired fitness score (AFS), guides candidate selection for in silico oracle evaluation. The policy is then updated by next-action cross-entropy imitation on the round's best oracle-labeled trajectories. Across eight in silico protein fitness landscapes and five strong baselines from prior work, SILO achieves competitive performance within the evaluated oracle budget, often demonstrating faster early-stage improvement than other reproduced baselines. Two-sided paired t-tests show positive mean differences in favor of SILO across all eight landscapes for both maximum fitness and top-100 mean fitness, with statistically significant improvements after Holm correction on two and four landscapes, respectively. Under low-labeled data and noisy-proxy conditions, SILO shows competitive, task-dependent performance. Ablations identify SBS as the primary driver of performance, while AFS guidance and iterative imitation provide complementary, task-dependent benefits within the oracle-budgeted optimization loop. Code is available at: https://github.com/grimmlab/SILO.git
